text:
Cam York has one assist in 11 games and the Flyers have scored 6.6 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice. That's one of the bigger luck gaps on the team, and our numbers flag him as due. He has also missed time, playing 11 of Philadelphia's 19 games.

Last season was his best by Evolving-Hockey's measure: 1.8 wins, 30th among defensemen, mostly from defense. They also noted his results ran ahead of his chances (0.8 expected wins), so some of that was hot goaltending or shooting. This year the pendulum has swung the other way.

The five-on-five picture is rough: 38% of the expected goals with him on, about five points worse than without. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the weak spot, with only 27% of his exits keeping possession, and NHL Edge has his top speed near the bottom tenth of the league. Our range says 13 to 28 points over a full season. The 2019 first-round pick plays over 20 minutes a night on a bad team. Some points will come back; the puck-moving needs to improve too.
headline: York is due for some luck
